faculty_summary: The Reliable Vision Lab studies uncertainty estimation and calibration for medical imaging models, with a focus on chest radiograph triage under distribution shift. Recent projects examine how calibration failures affect downstream clinical prioritization decisions.

faculty_summary_provenance.notes: Fictional professor for pipeline development. Do not use in analysis.

papers.title: Calibration Under Distribution Shift in Chest Radiograph Triage
papers.venue: Journal of Machine Learning for Health (fictional)
papers.abstract: Deep triage models for chest radiographs are typically evaluated in-distribution. We study calibration under realistic distribution shift across three hospital systems and find that expected calibration error increases up to threefold under scanner and population shift. A simple temperature-rescaling procedure applied per site recovers most of the loss on one benchmark dataset. We release evaluation code for site-stratified calibration.

papers.title: Do Uncertainty Estimates Help Radiologists Prioritize? A Retrospective Study
papers.abstract: We retrospectively evaluate whether model uncertainty estimates could help radiologists prioritize worklists. Using 12,000 historical chest radiographs from a single academic hospital, we simulate uncertainty-aware ordering and observe promising reductions in time-to-read for urgent findings. Results are retrospective and require prospective validation before clinical use.

papers.title: A Survey of Selective Prediction in Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: We survey selective prediction methods in medical imaging, categorizing abstention strategies, calibration approaches, and evaluation protocols, and identify open problems in site-transferable uncertainty estimation.

focal_passages.text: We evaluate three post-hoc calibration methods (temperature scaling, isotonic regression, and per-site temperature rescaling) on radiographs from three hospital systems, using site-held-out splits. No model retraining is performed; all interventions are post-hoc.
Per-site temperature rescaling reduced expected calibration error from 0.19 to 0.07 on the shifted benchmark, but gains did not transfer to the third hospital system, where ECE remained at 0.14.
